True Statement: Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands.
False 1: Exocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands.
FIB 1: ___ glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless glands.
FIB 2: Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ___ glands.
FIB 3: Endocrine glands lack ducts and hence are called ductless ___.
Reason: Endocrine (ductless) glands have no ducts; their secretions (hormones) are released directly into the surrounding tissue fluid and absorbed into the bloodstream.

True Statement: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
False 1: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in large amounts.
False 2: Hormones are nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
FIB 1: Hormones are ___ chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
FIB 2: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as ___ messengers and are produced in trace amounts.
FIB 3: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular ___ and are produced in trace amounts.
Reason: Hormones are not nutrients (they are not metabolised for energy); they act as chemical messengers, carrying signals between cells at very low concentrations.

True Statement: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and gonads.
False 1: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and liver.
FIB 1: ___ endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus and gonads.
FIB 2: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, ___, parathyroid, thymus and gonads.
FIB 3: Organised endocrine bodies include pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, ___, thymus and gonads.
Reason: The major endocrine glands include pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, pineal, thymus and gonads; each secretes specific hormones.

True Statement: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney and heart also produce hormones.
False 1: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, spleen, kidney and heart also produce hormones.
FIB 1: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the ___ tract, liver, kidney and heart also produce hormones.
FIB 2: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney and heart also ___ hormones.
FIB 3: In addition to organised endocrine glands, the gastrointestinal tract, liver, kidney and heart also produce ___.
Reason: The GI tract secretes gastrin, secretin, CCK and GIP; the liver secretes somatomedins; the kidney secretes erythropoietin; the heart secretes ANF.

True Statement: The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain.
False 1: The hypothalamus is the basal part of the cerebrum, forebrain.
False 2: The hypothalamus is the dorsal part of diencephalon, forebrain.
FIB 1: The ___ is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain.
FIB 2: The hypothalamus is the basal part of ___, forebrain.
FIB 3: The hypothalamus is the basal part of diencephalon, ___.
Reason: Hypothalamus is part of the diencephalon (thalamus + hypothalamus = diencephalon); it is the basal (floor) region of the diencephalon in the forebrain.

True Statement: The hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 1: The pineal gland contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate pituitary hormone synthesis and secretion.
FIB 1: The ___ contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones.
FIB 2: The hypothalamus contains ___ cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary hormones.
FIB 3: The hypothalamus contains neurosecretory cells called nuclei which produce hormones that regulate the synthesis and secretion of pituitary ___.
Reason: Neurosecretory nuclei in the hypothalamus synthesise peptide hormones that travel via the portal blood to the anterior pituitary to regulate its secretions.

True Statement: Hypothalamic releasing hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones.
False 1: Hypothalamic releasing hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones.
FIB 1: ___ releasing hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones.
FIB 2: Hypothalamic releasing hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones; ___ hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary hormones.
FIB 3: Hypothalamic releasing hormones stimulate secretion of pituitary hormones; inhibiting hormones inhibit secretion of pituitary ___.
Reason: Releasing hormones (e.g., GnRH, CRH, TRH, GHRH) stimulate pituitary hormone release; inhibiting hormones (e.g., somatostatin, dopamine) suppress it.

True Statement: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 1: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) inhibits pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
False 2: Somatostatin stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
FIB 1: ___ releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
FIB 2: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) ___ pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins.
FIB 3: Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates pituitary synthesis and release of ___.
Reason: GnRH (gonadotrophin releasing hormone) stimulates the pituitary gonadotrophs to release LH and FSH, which then act on the gonads.

True Statement: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 1: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus stimulates the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
False 2: GnRH inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
FIB 1: ___ from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
FIB 2: Somatostatin from the ___ inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary.
FIB 3: Somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the ___.
Reason: Somatostatin counteracts GHRH; it inhibits GH release by directly suppressing pituitary somatotroph cells.

True Statement: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
False 1: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through the lymphatic system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
False 2: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the posterior pituitary.
FIB 1: ___ hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
FIB 2: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal ___ system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary.
FIB 3: Hypothalamic hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior ___.
Reason: Hypothalamic hormones reach the anterior pituitary via a short portal vein system (hypothalamo-hypophyseal portal circulation), not the general circulation.

True Statement: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
False 1: The anterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
False 2: The pineal gland is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
FIB 1: The posterior ___ is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.
FIB 2: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural ___ of the hypothalamus.
FIB 3: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the ___.
Reason: The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) is connected to the hypothalamus by the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract (nerve axons); it is directly regulated by neural signals.

True Statement: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
False 1: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the thalamus by a stalk.
FIB 1: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella ___ and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
FIB 2: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is ___ to the hypothalamus by a stalk.
FIB 3: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the ___ by a stalk.
Reason: Sella turcica (Turkish saddle) is a depression in the sphenoid bone that cradles and protects the pituitary gland; the stalk (infundibulum) connects it to the hypothalamus.

True Statement: Pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars intermedia) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa = posterior pituitary).
False 1: Neurohypophysis consists of pars distalis and pars intermedia; adenohypophysis is pars nervosa.
False 2: Adenohypophysis includes pars nervosa; neurohypophysis includes pars distalis.
FIB 1: Pituitary is divided into ___ (pars distalis and pars intermedia) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa = posterior pituitary).
FIB 2: Pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars ___) and neurohypophysis (pars nervosa = posterior pituitary).
FIB 3: Pituitary is divided into adenohypophysis (pars distalis and pars intermedia) and ___ (pars nervosa = posterior pituitary).
Reason: Adenohypophysis (glandular anterior lobe) = pars distalis + pars intermedia; neurohypophysis (neural posterior lobe) = pars nervosa.

True Statement: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 1: Pars intermedia produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
False 2: Pars distalis produces only MSH.
FIB 1: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ___, LH and FSH.
FIB 2: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, ___ and FSH.
FIB 3: Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and ___.
Reason: Pars distalis cells produce six hormones: somatotrophs (GH), lactotrophs (PRL), thyrotrophs (TSH), corticotrophs (ACTH), gonadotrophs (LH and FSH).

True Statement: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone — melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
False 1: Pars distalis secretes only MSH.
False 2: Pars nervosa (neurohypophysis) secretes only MSH.
FIB 1: Pars ___ secretes only one hormone — melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).
FIB 2: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone — ___ stimulating hormone (MSH).
FIB 3: Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone — melanocyte ___ hormone (MSH).
Reason: Pars intermedia is a thin zone between anterior and posterior lobes; it secretes MSH, which acts on skin melanocytes.

True Statement: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.
False 1: Adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin synthesised by the hypothalamus.
False 2: Neurohypophysis stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are synthesised by the anterior pituitary.
FIB 1: ___ (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus.
FIB 2: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually ___ by the hypothalamus.
FIB 3: Neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the ___.
Reason: Oxytocin and ADH are synthesised by hypothalamic nuclei (paraventricular and supraoptic), transported down axons and stored in the neurohypophysis for release.

True Statement: Over-secretion of GH causes gigantism; low secretion of GH causes pituitary dwarfism.
False 1: Low secretion of GH causes gigantism; over-secretion of GH causes pituitary dwarfism.
FIB 1: ___ of GH causes gigantism; low secretion of GH causes pituitary dwarfism.
FIB 2: Over-secretion of GH causes gigantism; low secretion of ___ causes pituitary dwarfism.
FIB 3: Over-secretion of GH causes gigantism; low secretion of GH causes pituitary ___.
Reason: GH stimulates bone and muscle growth; in childhood, excess GH causes proportional overgrowth of all tissues (gigantism); deficiency impairs growth (pituitary dwarfism).

True Statement: Excess secretion of GH in adults (especially middle age) results in acromegaly — severe disfigurement especially of the face.
False 1: Excess secretion of prolactin in adults results in acromegaly.
False 2: Excess secretion of GH in adults results in gigantism.
FIB 1: Excess secretion of ___ in adults (especially middle age) results in acromegaly — severe disfigurement especially of the face.
FIB 2: Excess secretion of GH in adults (especially middle age) results in acromegaly — severe ___ especially of the face.
FIB 3: Excess secretion of GH in adults (especially middle age) results in acromegaly — severe disfigurement ___ of the face.
Reason: In adults, the epiphyseal plates are fused (no more linear bone growth); excess GH causes acromegaly — disproportionate enlargement of hands, feet and face.

True Statement: Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 1: Oxytocin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
False 2: TSH regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
FIB 1: ___ regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them.
FIB 2: Prolactin regulates the growth of the ___ glands and formation of milk in them.
FIB 3: Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and ___ of milk in them.
Reason: Prolactin (PRL) stimulates mammary gland development (lobuloalveolar growth) during pregnancy and milk synthesis (lactogenesis) postpartum.

True Statement: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 1: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
False 2: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
FIB 1: TSH ___ the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
FIB 2: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid ___ from the thyroid gland.
FIB 3: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the ___ gland.
Reason: TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) binds TSH receptors on thyroid follicular cells → activates adenylyl cyclase → increases T₃/T₄ synthesis and secretion.

True Statement: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 1: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
False 2: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.
FIB 1: ACTH ___ the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.
FIB 2: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of ___ from the adrenal cortex.
FIB 3: ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the ___ cortex.
Reason: ACTH (adrenocorticotrophic hormone) stimulates the adrenal cortex fasciculata zone to synthesise and secrete cortisol and other glucocorticoids.

True Statement: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
False 1: TSH and ACTH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
False 2: LH and FSH stimulate thyroid activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
FIB 1: LH and ___ stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins.
FIB 2: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal ___ and hence are called gonadotrophins.
FIB 3: LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called ___.
Reason: LH and FSH are gonadotrophins (gonad + trophin = nourishing the gonads); they stimulate gonadal growth, steroid synthesis and gametogenesis.

True Statement: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
False 1: In males, FSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
False 2: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the testis.
FIB 1: In males, ___ stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
FIB 2: In males, LH ___ the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.
FIB 3: In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of ___ from the testis.
Reason: In males, LH (= ICSH) binds Leydig cells, activating StAR and steroidogenic enzymes → testosterone synthesis.

True Statement: In males, FSH and androgens together regulate spermatogenesis.
False 1: In males, LH and androgens together regulate spermatogenesis.
False 2: In males, FSH and estrogens together regulate spermatogenesis.
FIB 1: In males, ___ and androgens together regulate spermatogenesis.
FIB 2: In males, FSH and androgens together ___ spermatogenesis.
FIB 3: In males, FSH and androgens together regulate ___.
Reason: FSH in males binds Sertoli cells and, together with intratubular testosterone, maintains spermatogenesis by supporting the developing germ cells.

True Statement: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 1: In females, FSH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.
False 2: In females, LH stimulates the growth and development of ovarian follicles.
FIB 1: In females, ___ induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.
FIB 2: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian ___ and maintains the corpus luteum.
FIB 3: In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and ___ the corpus luteum.
Reason: LH surge at mid-cycle triggers final oocyte maturation, rupture of the graafian follicle (ovulation), and formation + maintenance of the corpus luteum.

True Statement: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
False 1: LH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
False 2: ACTH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
FIB 1: FSH ___ growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females.
FIB 2: FSH stimulates growth and ___ of the ovarian follicles in females.
FIB 3: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in ___.
Reason: FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) stimulates growth of primordial follicles into growing follicles and induces aromatase activity (estrogen synthesis from androgens).

True Statement: MSH acts on melanocytes (melanin-containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 1: TSH acts on melanocytes and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
False 2: MSH acts on the adrenal cortex and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
FIB 1: MSH acts on ___ (melanin-containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
FIB 2: MSH acts on melanocytes (___ cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin.
FIB 3: MSH acts on melanocytes (melanin-containing cells) and regulates ___ of the skin.
Reason: MSH (melanocyte-stimulating hormone) binds MC1R on melanocytes, stimulating melanin synthesis and increasing skin pigmentation.

True Statement: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates vigorous contraction of the uterus at childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
False 1: Vasopressin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates uterus contraction and milk ejection.
False 2: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles; in females, it stimulates formation of milk (not milk ejection) from the mammary gland.
FIB 1: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it ___ vigorous contraction of the uterus at childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
FIB 2: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates vigorous ___ of the uterus at childbirth and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
FIB 3: Oxytocin acts on smooth muscles and stimulates their contraction; in females, it stimulates vigorous contraction of the uterus at ___ and milk ejection from the mammary gland.
Reason: Oxytocin binds receptors on uterine smooth muscle → Ca²⁺ signalling → strong contractions (parturition); also stimulates myoepithelial cells of mammary alveoli for milk ejection.

True Statement: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, reducing loss of water through urine.
False 1: Oxytocin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules.
False 2: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates loss of water through urine.
FIB 1: ___ (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, reducing loss of water through urine.
FIB 2: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates ___ of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules, reducing loss of water through urine.
FIB 3: Vasopressin (ADH) acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and ___ by the distal tubules, reducing loss of water through urine.
Reason: ADH (vasopressin) inserts aquaporin-2 channels into collecting duct cells → water reabsorption increases → concentrated urine → conserves body water.

True Statement: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 1: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of insulin results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
False 2: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in Diabetes Mellitus.
FIB 1: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ___ results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes Insipidus.
FIB 2: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called ___ Insipidus.
FIB 3: Impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in water loss and dehydration — a condition called Diabetes ___.
Reason: Without ADH, collecting ducts remain impermeable to water → large volumes of dilute urine (polyuria) and severe dehydration = Diabetes Insipidus.

True Statement: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
False 1: The pineal gland is located on the ventral side of the forebrain.
False 2: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the midbrain.
FIB 1: The pineal gland is ___ on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
FIB 2: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal ___ of the forebrain.
FIB 3: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the ___.
Reason: The pineal gland sits on the dorsal surface of the diencephalon (epithalamus); it receives light information from the retina via the SCN.

True Statement: Pineal secretes melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
False 1: Pineal secretes thymosins, which play an important role in the regulation of the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body.
False 2: Melatonin regulates blood calcium levels.
FIB 1: Pineal secretes melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a ___ (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
FIB 2: Pineal secretes melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the ___ cycle and body temperature.
FIB 3: Pineal secretes melatonin, which plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, including the sleep-wake cycle and body ___.
Reason: Melatonin is secreted at night (darkness) and suppressed by light; it entrains circadian rhythms (sleep-wake cycle) and seasonal reproductive cycles.

True Statement: Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
False 1: Vasopressin influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
FIB 1: Melatonin also influences ___, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
FIB 2: Melatonin also influences metabolism, ___, the menstrual cycle and defense capability.
FIB 3: Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defense ___.
Reason: Melatonin receptors in the SCN and other brain regions mediate its effects on circadian rhythms, core body temperature, and seasonal changes in reproductive physiology.

True Statement: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected by a thin flap of connective tissue called isthmus.
False 1: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the oesophagus, interconnected by isthmus.
False 2: The thyroid gland has two lobes interconnected by the corpus callosum.
FIB 1: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the trachea, ___ by a thin flap of connective tissue called isthmus.
FIB 2: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected by a thin flap of ___ tissue called isthmus.
FIB 3: The thyroid gland has two lobes located on either side of the trachea, interconnected by a thin flap of connective tissue called ___.
Reason: Thyroid's two lobes straddle the trachea (windpipe); they are joined by the isthmus (a fibrous bridge) over the front of the trachea.

True Statement: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (T₄/thyroxine) and triiodothyronine (T₃).
False 1: Parathyroid cells synthesise T₄ and T₃.
False 2: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise PTH and TCT.
FIB 1: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (___) and triiodothyronine (T₃).
FIB 2: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (T₄/thyroxine) and ___ (T₃).
FIB 3: Thyroid follicular cells synthesise two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (T₄/thyroxine) and triiodothyronine (___).
Reason: Iodination of tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin produces MIT and DIT; coupling gives T₃ (3 iodines) and T₄ (4 iodines) = thyroxine.

True Statement: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid.
False 1: Calcium is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the thyroid.
False 2: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of insulin synthesis in the pancreas.
FIB 1: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of ___ synthesis in the thyroid.
FIB 2: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone ___ in the thyroid.
FIB 3: Iodine is essential for the normal rate of hormone synthesis in the ___.
Reason: Iodine is built into the structure of T₃ and T₄; without adequate iodine, the thyroid cannot make enough hormone, so TSH rises and the gland enlarges (goitre).

True Statement: Deficiency of iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
False 1: Excess iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
False 2: Deficiency of iodine results in hyperthyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland.
FIB 1: ___ of iodine results in hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
FIB 2: Deficiency of iodine results in ___ and enlargement of the thyroid gland (goitre).
FIB 3: Deficiency of iodine results in hypothyroidism and ___ of the thyroid gland (goitre).
Reason: Iodine deficiency → insufficient T₃/T₄ → high TSH → TSH-driven thyroid cell proliferation → goitre; low T₃/T₄ also causes hypothyroidism symptoms.

True Statement: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism — stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism.
False 1: Hyperthyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism.
False 2: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes acromegaly.
FIB 1: ___ during pregnancy causes cretinism — stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism.
FIB 2: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism — stunted growth, mental retardation, low ___, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism.
FIB 3: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes cretinism — stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, ___.
Reason: Fetal and neonatal brain development requires T₃; without it, neural cell migration, myelination and synaptogenesis are impaired → irreversible cognitive deficit (cretinism).

True Statement: Hypothyroidism in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
False 1: Hyperthyroidism in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
FIB 1: ___ in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
FIB 2: Hypothyroidism in adult women may cause the ___ cycle to become irregular.
FIB 3: Hypothyroidism in adult women may cause the menstrual cycle to become ___.
Reason: T₃ is needed for normal pulsatile GnRH release; hypothyroidism disrupts the HPG axis → irregular or absent menstrual cycles.

True Statement: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
False 1: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hypothyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
False 2: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is characterised by decreased BMR and weight gain.
FIB 1: ___ goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
FIB 2: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, ___ of eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss.
FIB 3: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism characterised by thyroid enlargement, protrusion of eyeballs, increased ___ and weight loss.
Reason: Graves' disease: autoantibodies mimic TSH, continuously stimulating thyroid → excess T₃/T₄ → raised BMR, weight loss, heat intolerance, and exophthalmos (eye muscle expansion).

True Statement: Thyroid hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell formation.
False 1: Parathyroid hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate.
False 2: Thyroid hormones play an important role in regulating blood calcium levels.
FIB 1: ___ hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell formation.
FIB 2: Thyroid hormones play an important role in ___ the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell formation.
FIB 3: Thyroid hormones play an important role in regulating the basal metabolic rate and support the process of red blood cell ___.
Reason: T₃/T₄ increase the number and sensitivity of β-adrenergic receptors, upregulate mitochondrial enzymes → higher BMR; they also stimulate erythropoietin for RBC production.

True Statement: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.
False 1: Glucocorticoids control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.
FIB 1: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of ___, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and electrolyte balance.
FIB 2: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence ___ of water and electrolyte balance.
FIB 3: Thyroid hormones control the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and influence maintenance of water and ___ balance.
Reason: T₃/T₄ enter cells and bind nuclear thyroid hormone receptors → regulate transcription of metabolic enzyme genes controlling carbohydrate, fat and protein breakdown.

True Statement: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 1: The parathyroid gland secretes thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
False 2: The thyroid gland also secretes PTH which regulates blood calcium levels.
FIB 1: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called ___ (TCT) which regulates blood calcium levels.
FIB 2: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which ___ blood calcium levels.
FIB 3: The thyroid gland also secretes a protein hormone called thyrocalcitonin (TCT) which regulates blood ___ levels.
Reason: TCT (thyrocalcitonin) from parafollicular (C) cells of the thyroid lowers blood Ca²⁺ by inhibiting osteoclast activity and promoting Ca²⁺ deposition in bone.

True Statement: In humans, four parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland, one pair each in the two lobes of the thyroid gland.
False 1: In humans, two parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland.
